newsitem.title: USA: US Senate to study many telecom issues - lawmaker.
newsitem.headline: US Senate to study many telecom issues - lawmaker.

text.p: The new chairman of the Senate subcommittee on telecommunications said lawmakers plan to look at a variety of communications issues this year, including computer encryption, television liquor ads, TV program ratings, and airwave auctions.
"We'll be busy all year," Sen Conrad Burns, a Montana Republican, said in a speech to the Media Institute.
Burns said it was not yet clear how issues will be divvied up between his subcommittee and the full Commerce Committee, which is chaired by Sen John McCain, an Arizona Republican.
He did expect, however, that the full committee would hold hearings on spectrum auctions. McCain is a strong advocate of auctioning the airwaves to telecommunications providers.
In terms of liquor ads on television, Burns said he did not think it was the business of the Federal Communications Commission or the Federal Trade Commission to crack down on such ads.
But he did call on broadcasters to exercise responsibility on the matter. Lawmakers plan to hold hearings on that issue, as well as the TV industry's new system to rate programs.
Burns also suggested the system could end up prompting shows to contain more explicit sex and violence as a way to attract more viewers through racier ratings.
But he was not sure that would be the outcome. "I really hope it works," Burns said of the ratings system.

He said the V-chip technology mandated by Congress to accompany the ratings system was a bad idea. "To me, it's a bogus issue," said Burns. The technology, to be available in about a year, is intended to allow parents to screen out programs they do not want their children to watch.
